title: The Manifesto for Teaching and Learning in a Time of Generative AI: A Critical Collective Stance to Better Navigate the Future
extended_summary:
This paper is a manifesto-style critical collective article examining the implications of generative AI (GenAI), chatbots, and algorithms for higher education. Rather than testing an intervention, it addresses the broader question of how GenAI should be understood and governed in teaching and learning, emphasizing ethical, pedagogical, and social concerns alongside possible affordances. The paper is framed as a call for collective responsibility and evidence-based decision-making in response to the rapid rise of GenAI after the release of ChatGPT.

The approach is a qualitative collective-writing study using a modified Delphi process. The authors are worldwide educators and researchers in higher education with expertise in GenAI. Through anonymous open-ended prompts, coding, consensus-building, and member checking, they synthesized expert reflections into a set of positive and negative thematic statements about GenAI in education. These themes include time savings, personalized learning, lifelong learning, assessment redesign, innovation, accessibility, professional development, bias, academic integrity, misinformation, and over-reliance on technology.

The population described is higher education educators/researchers, not K-12 participants. The paper does not report a controlled implementation or student outcome study; instead, it offers a theoretical and normative framework for interpreting GenAI’s role in education. Its main conclusion is that GenAI is not neutral and should be integrated cautiously, with attention to equity, human oversight, transparency, and preservation of human values, critical thinking, and authentic learning.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI / large language model chatbot systems used for text and multimedia generation, question answering, feedback, tutoring, and content support.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper is a critical manifesto about generative AI in education and discusses GenAI/chatbots/LLMs at a conceptual level rather than evaluating a specific product.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an editorial/manifesto using collective writing and Delphi-style qualitative synthesis, not an empirical evaluation of an AI tool. It does not report controlled outcomes or subgroup analyses.
impact_tier_rationale: No intervention effects, effect sizes, or measured impacts are reported. The paper offers conceptual claims and critical reflections only.
